data.name: Samariah
data.gender_notes: Samariah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Samariah is a Hebrew name derived from the word 'shamar', which means 'to guard'. In the Bible, there is a city named Samaria, which was rebuilt by the Israelites after they returned from exile. The name Samariah could be interpreted as 'given by God' or 'protected by God'. The name Samariah carries the meaning “Given by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Samariah usually hope their child will grow to embody given by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name signifying trust in God's protection.
data.etymology: Samariah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Given by God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samariah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Samariah
in_english.meaning: a combination of Samuel meaning God has heard and Mariah meaning bitterness or wished-for child
in_english.long_meaning: The name Samariah originates from Hebrew roots combining Samuel (שמואל) meaning 'God has heard' and Mariah (מריה) meaning 'bitterness' or 'wished-for child'. It symbolizes one who is heard by God and is a wished-for child of God. Historically, it reflects a deep spiritual connection and significance in Christian tradition, embodying qualities of being divinely heard and loved.

data.cultural_impact: The name Samariah holds significant cultural impact, as it is a biblical name originating from the Hebrew language. In the ancient world, Samaria was a city located in the Northern Kingdom of Israel and was considered a symbol of religious and cultural diversity. It was the capital city of the Northern Kingdom during the time of the divided monarchy. The name Samariah also highlights the rich history of the Jewish people and their connection to their ancestral lands.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Samariah denotes protection and guardianship from God. It reminds us that God is always present in our lives and watches over us. The name can serve as a reminder of God's faithfulness and love, and can inspire us to trust in His care and protection. Samariah can also be seen as a reflection of the biblical story of the Israelites in Samaria, who, despite their struggles and hardships, continued to hold onto their faith and rebuild their city, ultimately receiving God's blessings. The name can be a source of strength and encouragement, inspiring us to trust in God and find hope in challenging times.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Samariah may represent the strength and resilience of a woman from the biblical city of Samaria. Her name carries the spiritual weight of the ancient city, a place of seeking and finding God amidst diverse cultures and peoples. May Samariah inspire us to embrace the complexities of life and remain steadfast in our faith.
